fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "An 800-Page Book That Landed in December 2019", "body": "Lester describes how What Really Makes You Ill? Why Everything You Thought You Knew About Disease Is Wrong grew out of a course she and co-author David Parker were running on the nature of reality, until the health section kept expanding into an almost 800 page tome with pages of references. They briefly considered splitting it into two smaller volumes, then kept it whole so readers could reach the second part on vested interests. Neither author has a medical background, which Lester frames as an advantage: no biases to overcome. Publication landed weeks before 2020, timing she calls divine guidance."}, {"title": "Reiki, a Reality Course, and a Mid-Nineties Wake-Up Call", "body": "Lester traces her path from a childhood spent at the window wondering about eternity, through years of reading she now reads as escapism, to a mid-1990s diagnosis she carefully calls the C word. She says she was frustrated and unhappy at the time, never fully committed to the system's authority, and knew the answer had something to do with mindset. Changes followed: leaving a marriage, a local center, a reiki class that immediately drew her in, and David's course, parts of which felt like something she already knew. Garton hears the shape of a shamanic healing crisis, a hero's journey with information brought back for the tribe."}, {"title": "The Case Lester Makes Against the Disease Model", "body": "Lester argues that labels turn processes into things, that a symptom in one part need not mean anything is wrong with that part, and that the body drifts around homeostasis rather than sitting inside a narrow band. She calls the lab's normal range arbitrary, notes that blood pressure readings run high because people are nervous, and points to Bruce Lipton's work for the claim that genes do not control biology. She mentions German New Medicine and the asbestos and mesothelioma link without treating either as a total answer. Garton's outro reports her Substack citations: Leverson's 1911 London lecture, Bailey's 1928 London Medical World article, Stefan Lanka, and Virus Mania."}, {"title": "The Ancestral River and a Client Half a World Away", "body": "Garton walks through a recent biofield tuning with a New Zealand client whose digestive blockages triggered a racing heart. He was pulled instead to the crown chakra and the zone he calls the ancestral river, where he read a paternal grandmother raising small children in poverty and fear. The client confirmed a grandmother in London through World War Two, husband away, bombs overhead. Because stuck energy sits further from the body the older it is, roughly ten inches out, maternal on the left and paternal on the right, he floats a theory that the 2020 to 2022 charge transited that river. Lester calls it worth investigating."}, {"title": "Fear, Word Magic, and Where to Find Dawn", "body": "The through line Lester names for two years of writing at dawnlester.substack.com, titled Dawn's Writings, is helping people come away from fear that is unnecessary, since frightened people stop thinking. Both speakers turn to language: Garton notes that screen once meant separating the worthless from the valuable, from the Latin cerno, and that a victim is literally a living being sacrificed to a deity, with the state as the modern deity. Lester's answer to division is conversation without any need to convince. Garton's outro draws a parallel he sees between germ fear and climate fear, two invisible boogeymen. Lester was headed to Music and Sky as a speaker."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Dawn Lester, researcher and author about the connections between consciousness & health, joins InnerVerse for a free-flowing conversation, wherein we discuss the importance of her book, What Really Makes You Ill, and the inspiration behind it, how a healing crisis set Dawn on her spiritual path, alternate interpretations of major illnesses, the flawed nature of prevailing disease theories, ancestral rivers and potential biofield transits with world events, and breaking victimhood mindsets.
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: In the Plus+ Extension, we talk about the demonization of the Sun, transcending resistance to emotions, why diagnosis labels are antithetical to health, how to attend to the body's message within discomfort, possibilities of weather warfare, whether or not reality is an illusion, humours and internal/external waters, and what to make of the secret spells in the word magic of English. All that and more!

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The Sun Recast as a Threat", "body": "Chance opens the extension with Dawn's Substack piece on demonizing the sun, calling the sun the obvious source of light, warmth and energy in the world. Dawn explains that she pulls headlines from the BBC website to answer what she calls the latest propaganda, and that this story blamed sunshine alone for rising melanoma while leaning on one personal case for sympathy. In her view a single cause is never the whole picture, so she points to terrain, diet, hydration and the chemical ingredients in sunscreen, then ties the scare to climate messaging and geoengineering talk of blotting out the sun, an inversion of something she calls life."}, {"title": "Finding the Opposite Inside a Feeling", "body": "Chance describes a consciousness shift on a hot day when, instead of resisting the heat, he put his attention into it and found coolness inside, then spent the next winter looking for warmth in the cold until barefoot walks in snow became possible. He frames it as a hermetic polarity and says emotions work the same way, that resisting a feeling does the most harm, and that joy sits inside sadness and excitement inside anxiety. Dawn admits she is no fan of the cold, then adds that naming a feeling turns it into a thing, while sitting with it unlabelled gives the full experience."}, {"title": "Pain as a Message, Listening as Medicine", "body": "Drawing on biofield tuning, Chance says a repressed emotion has to be made conscious and felt, and that the worst move afterward is handing it a label and a story, since the mind quickly decides the feeling means you are no good. His test is a stubbed toe: put full attention into the pain and the intensity changes, like finally answering a man who keeps shouting hey. Dawn agrees even a stubbed toe carries a message. When Chance links healing to helios, light and attention, she contrasts that with a system built on suppression, recalls doctors whose bedside manner meant listening, and cites John Sarno's book on back pain."}, {"title": "Fear Campaigns and a Thought Based Reality", "body": "Chance asks whether weather is the next fear campaign, noting talk of climate lockdowns, a Twisters sequel and a stormy American spring, and wondering whether his own attention feeds what he sees. Dawn says she holds no strong views but sees several scares being tried at once, like a horse race with no clear leader, and reads the climate push as making people afraid of nature so they leave the land for smart cities. She adds that talk of a disease X has even casual observers calling it rubbish. Reality, she says, is created and thought based without being an illusion, and it mirrors beliefs back as feedback."}, {"title": "Allusion, Humor and Word Magic", "body": "Chance proposes that reality is less an illusion than an allusion, everything perceived pointing back to the inner world, and offers a stranger's barbershop T-shirt turning up as he weighed a spontaneous haircut. Dawn likes the change of word and says the creator has a sense of humor. Chance then traces humor to moisture, the old medical humors, and waters above and below the firmament. Dawn wonders whether that redeems the word human, and both agree intent outweighs fear of hidden meanings: she sees no ill intent in saying understand in everyday speech, and Chance passes along Amandha Vollmer's habit of saying dawning instead of morning."}]

fields.Plus Quotes JSON: [{"text": "The sun, its energy is consciousness. I mean that quite literally, because without the sun's light, we would be conscious of nothing in our environment.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "It's the resisting of a feeling that causes the most harm.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "In my articles, I've tended to refer to them as the would be controllers, 'cause they would like to control us, but that doesn't mean they're going to.", "author": "Dawn Lester", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/9e57510a-e6f7-4b8d-8d75-3a94613f90cb/DAWN-LESTER.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "The pain or the emotional pain is all just information. It's a signal from your body trying to get your attention to a certain part of your body or a certain part of your psyche.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Sometimes even something like stubbing your toe is you trying to communicate with yourself.", "author": "Dawn Lester", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/9e57510a-e6f7-4b8d-8d75-3a94613f90cb/DAWN-LESTER.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "I think a lot of people have lost the art of truly listening, truly hearing a person so that they feel listened to, feel heard.", "author": "Dawn Lester", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/9e57510a-e6f7-4b8d-8d75-3a94613f90cb/DAWN-LESTER.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Everything you see at all times, everything you perceive is alluding to what your inner world is doing all the time.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "When we trap ourselves in the beliefs, we will then see those beliefs kind of reflected back out.", "author": "Dawn Lester", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/9e57510a-e6f7-4b8d-8d75-3a94613f90cb/DAWN-LESTER.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Don't get caught up in the secret spells of English language. As much as I like learning about the variety of meanings, I still think intent carries the day.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "It's a time when we are shifting out of an old belief system into a completely new paradigm.", "author": "Dawn Lester", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/9e57510a-e6f7-4b8d-8d75-3a94613f90cb/DAWN-LESTER.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}]
fields.Quotes JSON: [{"text": "You shouldn't have to put the word real in front of science, but I think more and more of us are realising that it's become scientism.", "author": "Dawn Lester", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/9e57510a-e6f7-4b8d-8d75-3a94613f90cb/DAWN-LESTER.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "You guys are probably the poster children for why there were articles coming out during cooties that said why it's not safe to do your own research.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "And to be able to take the control back is very empowering. It does require responsibility as well.", "author": "Dawn Lester", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/9e57510a-e6f7-4b8d-8d75-3a94613f90cb/DAWN-LESTER.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "That's the whole problem with reductionism in general is trying to boil everything down to almost programming code of if this, then that.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "They have a set of results that they call the normal range. And that's arbitrary. There is nobody in the world who is normal.", "author": "Dawn Lester", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/9e57510a-e6f7-4b8d-8d75-3a94613f90cb/DAWN-LESTER.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "The original meaning of the word screen is to separate the worthless from the valuable.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "We are influenced by everything. We're connected to everything. We are all absolutely interconnected and we are individual and interconnected at the same time.", "author": "Dawn Lester", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/9e57510a-e6f7-4b8d-8d75-3a94613f90cb/DAWN-LESTER.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "The invisible boogeyman is changing the climate. The invisible boogeyman is spreading the germ. Do you see the similarity here?", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}]
